guard: operator color follows FORCE_COLOR first, then a non-empty NO_COLOR, then stdout.isTTY, and every c.* helper and color256 asks on each call
why: The suite imports colors.ts from src through tsx, so a mutation is seen without a build and needs no rebuild after the restore.
Each mutation is compile-clean and its anchor occurs exactly once in the named file.

mutations.name: W1 FORCE_COLOR is ignored
mutations.note: Without the first check a pinned FORCE_COLOR does nothing, which is the state the status-persona-root smoke's pin was in before.

mutations.name: W2 FORCE_COLOR=false counts as on
mutations.expectRed: FORCE_COLOR=false on a TTY is plain
mutations.cell: FORCE_COLOR=false on a TTY is plain
mutations.note: Node treats `false` like `0`; only the TTY case can see it, because a non-TTY is already plain.

mutations.name: W3 NO_COLOR wins over FORCE_COLOR
mutations.note: The order is the contract: FORCE_COLOR decides first, as Node does.

mutations.name: W4 NO_COLOR is ignored
mutations.expectRed: NO_COLOR=1 on a TTY is plain
mutations.cell: NO_COLOR=1 on a TTY is plain
mutations.note: On a non-TTY the TTY check already turns color off, so only the TTY case can see NO_COLOR dropped.

mutations.name: W5 piped stdout keeps its color
mutations.note: The original bug in #2381: escapes in pipes and log files.

mutations.name: W6 the helpers stop asking
mutations.expectRed: NO_COLOR=1 on a TTY is plain
mutations.cell: NO_COLOR=1 on a TTY is plain
mutations.note: colorEnabled() can be right while the helpers ignore it; this is the shape main had before #2405.
